title: Singleton

act2.summary: the suite needs two configurations live in the same run

solutions.title: An explicit createPressRoom(settings) factory, no shared instance
solutions.tradeoff: Any number of independent press rooms can exist at once, each built from its own explicit settings - the thing a singleton is specifically built to make impossible. The price: there is no longer a single, well-known place every part of the app is guaranteed to agree with; two press rooms built from two different settings will happily disagree, and nothing stops a caller from building an unwanted second one by accident.

reviewFocus: Does anything in solutions/module-and-injection/ still read from a shared, module-level mutable variable the way src/settings.ts's `instance` does?
Could two independently-built press rooms ever accidentally end up sharing the same settings object by reference, defeating the isolation this route exists to provide?
Is `mainFloor` itself still a singleton in every sense that matters - and if so, what did this refactor actually change?
Read WALKTHROUGH.md's DESIGN.md §9.2 paragraph before deciding this verdict is settled: is there a real case, in THIS codebase, where the shared instance was the right call?
